items.title: Lovie Austin Interview, 1969-04-25
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I knew John Steiner told me you were playing piano for a dance studio.

ctx.x: Well, I went to work at the Monogram in 1913. In 13? And I worked at 34th Street until they moved to 35th Street, and I moved there with him. That's the first time I went to New York, and I came right back and stayed down there when I worked there 25 years straight. And then I went to New York and started working for Herdic and Seaman. I was taking high fast shows, and I worked for Herdic and Seaman for a long time. And then I came, when I came home, my mother died in 31. So I just came on the stage. You stayed…
I knew John Steiner told me you were playing piano for a dance studio.

Yeah, Jimmy Payne. Then I worked for him 17 years. Yes, I knew you'd been there. And then I worked for another woman, a white woman who had a studio down there at Jackson Boulevard, 22, East Jackson. Oh, yes. And then I got sick. I was in the hospital for four or five months, and I came out. My sister just died in November, in April. She'd been there almost two years now. Well, she had been there two years. Yes, you think this is that you have. So I haven't been doing anything since my sister died. I just stayed…
